findings.text: The fence is recorded only as a scalar triple, with no geometry for the row it was measured on. The node's own follow-on says the floor drifted 22% on the current moment (2.92403e-16 at d9b594b2 to 2.26749e-16 here), but a reader cannot test that cause from the artifact: the weak-110 fence row's cut_cells and realised_cells are not stored, so there is no way to see whether the clip's arc sampling changed. Storing the fence row's cut_cells/realised_cells, as the moment-floor schema already does, would let a reader see whether the geometry moved rather than only that the scalar did.

The row error is measured against the quadratic-density fan (_fan_quadratic_density_moments at benchmarks/exact_clip_closed_form_floor.py:248, order 16) while the fence is the true-density fan's own refinement floor (_fan_cut_moments at benchmarks/exact_clip_moment_floor.py:690, order 16 vs order 8). These are two different fan integrals - one integrates a fitted quadratic, the other the true density at the rule points - so the fence bounds the true-density fan's refinement noise, not the refinement noise of the reference the row error is taken against. The verdicts are still the decision's, but the record presents the margin as route-vs-fence in one norm without saying the two arms differ.

All five verdicts sit at the round-off scale and are decided by floating-point ordering, not by a physical representation error. The fence's current value is 2.26749e-16 (about one machine epsilon) and the five current errors are 1.73051e-16, 2.01362e-16, 2.06993e-16, 2.29975e-16 and 2.96282e-16 - all within a factor 1.3 of the fence, so a pass or a fail here is one ULP-ordering apart. The record flags only moderate-1000 as marginal, but the three passing rows and the strong-110 failure are equally round-off-scale and should carry the same caveat; otherwise the record reads as a settled accuracy result when the decision's accepted cost (the fence is only as tight as the fan's own refinement floor) makes it an ordering at the round-off scale.
